initial_blocks.learning_goal: Teach novice stockroom coordinators a simple reorder-point rule. Explain the logic, work through an example, then offer a short practice exercise with its answer.
initial_blocks.rule: Reorder point = daily demand x lead time in days + safety stock. Inventory position = on-hand + on-order - committed. Place an order when inventory position is less than or equal to the reorder point.
initial_blocks.worked_example: Daily demand 15 units; lead time 5 days; safety stock 22 units. Reorder point 97 units. Explain each arithmetic step and label units.
initial_blocks.inventory: On-hand 89, on-order 20, committed 17: inventory position 92. It is below reorder point 97, so ORDER. Target position 197; order quantity 105. Preserve on-order and committed values.
initial_blocks.process: Connected decision: read counts -> calculate inventory position -> compare with reorder point -> ORDER if at/below, otherwise WAIT. The WAIT branch returns to the next daily review.
initial_blocks.practice: Exercise: inventory position 109; reorder point 97. Answer WAIT, because the position is 12 units above the trigger. Reveal answer on the slide following the exercise.
initial_blocks.misconceptions: Do not compare on-hand alone with the trigger. Do not multiply safety stock by lead time. A larger reorder point is a trigger, not the order quantity.
initial_blocks.checklist: Before ordering: verify units, include existing orders, subtract commitments, then check the trigger. Use a simple annotated number line built with editable text and lines.
